after.notes: Due to the popularity of the Bridge Watch Rating program, only completed applications, with the required documents, will be considered. Scheduled intakes March, September and December *Scheduled intakes are subject to change. Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Note: Applicants to this program must be 18 years of age by the time the intake begins. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet all entrance requirements and will be accepted on a first-qualified basis as long as space remains. When available intakes are full, qualified applicants are wait-listed. Applicants must meet all entrance requirements prior to applying to this program. If you are uncertain, or don’t meet the requirements, we strongly recommend you complete any applicable Trades Entry Assessments before applying. English language proficiency: one of: Category 3 – English Studies 12 (50%) or equivalent or BCIT English Trades Entry Assessment Math: one of the following: Pre-Calculus 11 (50%) or Foundations of Math 11 (50%) or Workplace Math 11 (50%) or Other acceptable BC and Yukon courses or BCIT Math Trades Entry Assessment Medical certificate from a Transport Canada-approved physician * *The Marine Medical must be for the Deck Service Occupation. Medicals for catering or other occupations are not accepted. Students must be at least 18 years of age by the time the intake begins Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Additional requirements All students need to complete Transport Canada’s Fatigue Management at Sea (FMT) training prior to the MEDI courses. Please email a copy of your completed training certificate to your Program Assistant/Program Coordinator and Department Head prior to the MEDI course start date. Be prepared to present a physical copy of your FMT certificate on the 1st day of the course at the BCIT Marine Campus (BMC) or Justice Institute of BC (JIBC). In order to complete the firefighting portion of MEDI 1510 – STCW Basic Safety Training and MEDI 2510 – Advanced Fire Fighting, participants must be clean-shaven where the self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA) or any tight-fitting respirator seals with the face, as per WorkSafe BC Occupational Health and Safety Regulation Part 31: Firefighting . Students must follow the rules and regulations provided by BCIT and the Justice Institute of BC for the donning of personal protective equipment. Recommended for success It is strongly recommended that applicants have high school graduation. International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks.
